Bilateral ductal or vascular involvement, inadequate
Selected early perihilar CCA — Mayo protocol:
Cholangiocarcinoma is classified by site: intrahepatic (hepatectomy), perihilar / Klatskin (extended hepatectomy + caudate
lobe + bile-duct excision + hepaticojejunostomy), and distal (Whipple).
The caudate lobe (segment I) is routinely resected in perihilar cholangiocarcinoma because its ducts drain directly into the
Bismuth-Corlette grades hilar ductal extent (I below the confluence → IV both ducts) and guides the side of hepatectomy —
don't confuse it with the Bismuth bile-duct-injury classification.
CA19-9 is not specific — it rises with benign biliary obstruction and cholangitis, so interpret it after biliary decompression.
Optimise the future liver remnant (portal vein embolisation + drainage of the remnant) before a major hepatectomy to avoid
PSC is the strongest Western risk factor — new jaundice or a dominant stricture in PSC is cholangiocarcinoma until proven
otherwise; transplant (Mayo protocol) suits selected early perihilar disease, not intrahepatic.
Sources: Bismuth-Corlette classification (perihilar cholangiocarcinoma) · AJCC 8th edition (separate T staging for intrahepatic / perihilar / distal). Adjuvant: BILCAP (capecitabine).
Advanced: ABC-02 (gemcitabine + cisplatin) and TOPAZ-1 (adds durvalumab). Transplant: Mayo Clinic protocol.
Extended hepatectomy for perihilar CCA includes the caudate lobe (segment I) + extrahepatic bile-duct excision + hepaticojejunostomy + portal lymphadenectomy. GB cancer &
choledochal cysts are on biliary sheet 2; bile-duct injury is on sheet 4.
